outcome: No proof of Leopoldt's conjecture for general number fields has appeared since 26 January 2024. The in-window events are a conditional reduction (Dasgupta and Kakde, Aug 2024: a p-adic Matrix Coefficient Conjecture would imply Leopoldt) and a conditional paper on a different, non-abelian conjecture (Barrera Salazar, Graham and Williams, Mar 2026). Earlier partial results include Ferri and Johnston's non-abelian S3 families at prescribed finite sets of primes (posted Jan 2023, journal 2026). Mihailescu's claims of proof for CM fields and for all number fields (2009 to 2016) are withdrawn in part or unrefereed, and no public check of them was found.
problem_asks: Statement: for a number field K and a prime p, the p-adic regulator of K (built from p-adic logarithms of a basis of the units; equivalently the Leopoldt defect delta(K,p)) does not vanish. Parts: (1) every number field K, not only totally real or CM fields (Leopoldt's own definition covers totally real and CM fields only; for other fields the statement is put as equality of the Z-rank and Z_p-rank of the units, i.e. delta(K,p)=0); (2) every prime p, since the statement names none and so is quantified over all primes; (3) the conclusion is non-vanishing of the regulator, equivalently delta(K,p)=0, i.e. the closure of the global units in the local principal units has Z_p-rank r1+r2-1. Equivalent reformulation named in the sources (Colmez, for totally real F): the p-adic zeta function of F has a simple pole at s=1. Not asked: any particular field, bound, or special case.

events.what_happened: Brumer proved Leopoldt's conjecture for abelian extensions of Q and of imaginary quadratic fields, after Ax (1965) reduced the abelian case to a p-adic version of Baker's theorem, which Brumer then proved (the Baker-Brumer theorem). Journal: Mathematika 14 (1967), per the Wikipedia citation list; the paper itself was not opened.
events.delivers: Leopoldt at every prime p for every finite abelian extension K of Q, and for every finite abelian extension of an imaginary quadratic field. Source wording differs on whether CM fields with abelian maximal real subfield are also covered; I did not resolve this.
events.remains: Every non-abelian number field (over Q or over an imaginary quadratic field), and every field outside the abelian cases, at every prime.

checked_by.who: Armand Brumer (author); the result is treated as settled in the standard literature cited by Wikipedia (Ax 1965, Brumer 1967, Neukirch-Schmidt-Wingberg 2008, Washington 1997)
checked_by.qualification: Author of the proof; the textbook citations were not opened
checked_by.what_they_did: Published the proof in Mathematika (1967); later texts cite it as settled

events.direction: Consistent with the conjecture (proves it for a restricted class of fields).

events.what_happened: Waldschmidt's transcendence bound on the Leopoldt defect: the defect delta(K,p) is at most (number of archimedean places of K minus 1)/2, i.e. at most half the unit rank. Reported as a cited result in Maksoud (arXiv 2201.08203, opened). Waldschmidt's own paper was not opened, and the sources give 1981 or 1984 for it.
events.delivers: A general upper bound on the defect for every number field and every prime. Read as an integer bound, it forces delta=0 whenever r1+r2 is at most 2 (unit rank at most 1). That consequence is my deduction from the form of the bound quoted by Maksoud, not a statement made by a source. It gives nothing for fields with r1+r2 at least 3.
events.remains: Leopoldt for every field with r1+r2 at least 3, at every prime.
events.direction: Partial bound in the conjectured direction (defect tends to zero), not a zero-defect result for any field outside the small-unit-rank cases.

events.what_happened: Buchmann and Sands, 'Leopoldt's conjecture in parameterized families' (Proc. AMS 104 (1988) 43-48, per the AMS listing title seen in search; not opened), together with their 1987 J. Number Theory algorithm paper. A search summary quoting Ferri and Johnston's survey gives two families of quintic fields with Galois closure S5: for lambda a root of x^5+4A^4x+1 (A at least 1), Leopoldt holds at every p not 5 dividing 2A; for lambda a root of x^5-B^4x+1 (B at least 2), at every p not 5 dividing B. Units from Maus.
events.delivers: Leopoldt at the stated primes for two infinite families of non-abelian quintic fields with S5 Galois closure (non-totally-real in the cited family, per the survey summary).
events.remains: All other fields of these shapes, all primes outside the stated sets, and all other fields.
events.direction: Consistent with the conjecture for the named families and primes.

events.what_happened: J. W. Sands, 'Kummer's and Iwasawa's version of Leopoldt's conjecture', Canadian Mathematical Bulletin. The Cambridge page gives online publication 20 Nov 2018 and copyright 1988; the year 1988 is used here, with the discrepancy noted. Abstract as seen in search: refines Iwasawa's approach and shows that Leopoldt for K carries over to certain solvable extensions L of K under conditions on the degree and discriminant of K and on a class-number quotient. Not opened.
events.delivers: A reduction: Leopoldt for K implies Leopoldt for certain solvable extensions L of K under stated conditions. No unconditional new field.
events.remains: Leopoldt for K itself, and for all L outside the stated conditions.
events.direction: Reduction in the conjectured direction; conditional on the base field's conjecture.

events.what_happened: Jaulent, a French note on arXiv (0712.2995, 2007) claiming that number fields of arbitrary degree with weak ramification satisfy the Leopoldt conjecture on the l-adic rank of the units. Known only from a search snippet of the abstract; not opened. The arXiv number suggests December 2007, but the month is not confirmed, so only the year is given.
events.delivers: As claimed: Leopoldt at every prime for fields of arbitrary degree satisfying a weak-ramification hypothesis (the hypothesis's exact form is not recorded here).
events.remains: Fields that are not weakly ramified.
events.time_since_posted: about 19 years; no engagement located in the searches run here (engagement was not searched for specifically)
events.doubts: Not opened. The claim appears in one note with no later reading located.
events.direction: Consistent with the conjecture, if the claim holds, for a restricted class.

events.what_happened: Mihailescu, 'The T and T* components of Lambda-modules and Leopoldt's conjecture' (arXiv 0905.1274; v1 8 May 2009, v2 27 Jun 2009, v3 15 Sep 2009, v4 20 Sep 2010, v5 17 Feb 2015 withdrawn). The abstract as displayed on the arXiv page says 'We prove both conjectures for arbitrary number fields', i.e. Leopoldt and Gross-Kuz'min, and states that Gross-Kuz'min is dual to Leopoldt under the Iwasawa involution. The v5 withdrawal comment reads 'Withdrawn - the material was expanded in individual papers on the Conjectures of Leopoldt, Iwasawa and Gross, all on arxive after 2014'. The displayed abstract may come from v4; whether v1 (8 May 2009) carried the same general claim was not checked.
events.revisions: v1 8 May 2009; v2 27 Jun 2009; v3 15 Sep 2009; v4 20 Sep 2010; v5 17 Feb 2015 (withdrawn, 1 KB).
events.delivers: As claimed in the abstract: Leopoldt's conjecture for every number field, at every prime. No proof text was read.
events.remains: Nothing, if the claim held. The paper is withdrawn, so no current version carries it.
events.time_since_posted: about 17 years since v1; withdrawn Feb 2015
events.doubts: Withdrawn by the author in Feb 2015. The later papers the withdrawal points to (1403.7331, 1105.4544) treat only CM fields, so the general claim is not carried forward in any non-withdrawn paper found. No published critique or referee report was located.

withdrawn.what: Whole paper (v5, 1 KB). Comment: 'Withdrawn - the material was expanded in individual papers on the Conjectures of Leopoldt, Iwasawa and Gross, all on arxive after 2014'.

events.direction: Claims a proof in the conjectured direction (for all number fields); withdrawn.

events.what_happened: Mihailescu, 'Applications of Baker Theory to the Conjecture of Leopoldt' (arXiv 0909.2738; v1 15 Sep 2009, v2 20 Oct 2009, v3 17 Feb 2015 withdrawn). The displayed abstract claims 'a short, elementary proof of the following too extreme cases of the Leopoldt conjecture': K/Q solvable (first proof by Baker theory) and K/Q totally real with p split completely (second proof by class field theory). Withdrawn comment on the v3 record: 'Outdated approach to Leopoldt, replaced by Version from March 2014'. Whether v1 carried the same claims was not checked.
events.revisions: v1 15 Sep 2009; v2 20 Oct 2009; v3 17 Feb 2015 (withdrawn, 1 KB).
events.delivers: As claimed: Leopoldt at every prime for every solvable Galois extension K/Q (this includes non-abelian solvable fields), and for totally real K/Q at primes that split completely in K.
events.remains: Non-solvable Galois extensions of Q, non-totally-real fields, and primes not split completely in the second class.
events.time_since_posted: about 17 years since v1; withdrawn Feb 2015
events.doubts: Withdrawn by the author, who calls the approach outdated. The 'replacement' the comment names is dated March 2014, but the March 2014 paper (1403.7331) concerns CM fields, so it is unclear what replaces the solvable-case claim. No published critique was located.

withdrawn.what: Whole paper (v3). Comment: 'Outdated approach to Leopoldt, replaced by Version from March 2014'.

events.direction: Claims partial proofs in the conjectured direction (restricted classes); withdrawn.

events.what_happened: Mihailescu, 'Leopoldt's Conjecture for CM fields' (arXiv 1105.4544; v1 23 May 2011, v2 9 Jun 2011, v3 17 Feb 2015 withdrawn with no reason given, v4 17 Feb 2016 current). Current v4 states: 'We prove this conjecture for CM number fields K'. Argument (as paraphrased in the listing and in a search snippet): if Leopoldt failed for a CM field K, build an auxiliary CM Z_p-extension in which certain split primes give a contradiction. The proof relies on the vanishing of mu for CM Z_p-extensions, which the author proves in separate papers listed on his arXiv page (1105.1970 and 1409.3114; not opened). An appendix is said to complete the argument without assuming mu=0.
events.revisions: v1 23 May 2011; v2 9 Jun 2011; v3 17 Feb 2015 (withdrawn, 1 KB); v4 17 Feb 2016 (current, 29 KB).
events.delivers: As claimed: Leopoldt at every prime for every CM number field K (a search snippet says odd p only; the abstract page does not restrict p). Nothing for non-CM fields.
events.remains: Every non-CM number field, at every prime.
events.time_since_posted: about 15 years since v1; about 10 years since current v4. No referee report, journal acceptance or published critique located.
events.doubts: (1) The author withdrew v3 in Feb 2015 with no reason and re-posted v4 in Feb 2016. (2) The argument depends on mu=0 for CM Z_p-extensions, which the author proves in companion arXiv papers; I did not read those. (3) A 2021 listing titled 'A Conditional Proof of the Leopoldt Conjecture for CM Fields' by the same author, found only on sugaku.net, suggests the unconditional claim was later recast as conditional; it is not in the arXiv listing and its condition is unknown (see the 2021 event). (4) Wikipedia (last edited 21 July 2026, per the fetch summary) says Mihailescu 'announced a proof of Leopoldt's conjecture for all CM-extensions of Q', which differs from the paper's 'CM number fields K'.

withdrawn.what: v3 (Feb 2015) withdrawn with no reason given; v4 (Feb 2016) is current and repeats the CM claim.

events.direction: Claims a proof in the conjectured direction for CM fields; withdrawn-then-reposted; the stated proof depends on a companion claim (mu=0).

events.what_happened: Dawn C. Nelson, 'A Variation on Leopoldt's Conjecture: Some Local Units instead of All Local Units' (arXiv 1308.4637, single version, 21 Aug 2013). Asks whether the Z_p-rank of the diagonal image of the global units is controlled when they are mapped into some local units rather than all of them; answers affirmatively using the p-adic Schanuel conjecture. It does not prove Leopoldt. A search summary attributed this paper to Mihailescu; the arXiv abstract page names Nelson as sole author.
events.delivers: A variant of the conjecture (projection to some local units), conditional on the p-adic Schanuel conjecture. Says nothing unconditional about Leopoldt's conjecture as stated.
events.remains: The conjecture as stated (all local units), unconditionally, for every field and prime.
events.doubts: Conditional on p-adic Schanuel, which is itself open.
events.direction: An analogue (different hypotheses and a different embedding); neither for nor against the conjecture as stated.

events.what_happened: Mihailescu, 'The Leopoldt and Iwasawa Conjectures for CM fields' (arXiv 1403.7331; single version submitted 28 Mar 2014). Abstract: for a CM field K and a CM Z_p-extension L/K, the Iwasawa mu-invariant of L vanishes; for L cyclotomic this is Iwasawa's mu=0 conjecture; if L is not cyclotomic, Leopoldt fails for K, and an auxiliary CM Z_p-extension with mu not zero then gives a contradiction, 'showing that the Leopoldt conjecture must hold for CM fields'. The abstract says the paper supersedes earlier versions that attempted parts of the result.
events.revisions: v1 28 Mar 2014 only (the sole listed version).
events.delivers: As claimed: Leopoldt at every prime for every CM field K. The same abstract also claims mu=0 for every CM Z_p-extension, including the cyclotomic one.
events.remains: Every non-CM number field, at every prime.
events.time_since_posted: about 12 years 6 months. No referee report, journal acceptance or published critique located.
events.doubts: (1) The claimed cyclotomic case is Iwasawa's mu=0 conjecture for CM fields. My understanding (not verified in this run) is that this is open in general, since Ferrero-Washington covers abelian extensions of Q; if the paper proves it, the paper's claim is far larger than the Leopoldt statement, and this is a reason to scrutinise the argument. (2) Single listed version with no comments. (3) The same author's earlier general claim (2009) and CM claim (2011) were withdrawn or reposted, and this paper says it supersedes earlier attempts.
events.direction: Claims a proof in the conjectured direction for CM fields, together with a stronger mu=0 statement.

events.what_happened: Khare and Thorne, 'Potential automorphy and the Leopoldt conjecture' (arXiv 1409.7007; v1 24 Sep 2014, v2 6 Jul 2016 marked 'to appear in AJM'). Studies Hida's p-adic Hecke algebra for GL_n over a CM field. The automorphy-lifting result is conditional on the existence and local-global compatibility of Galois representations attached to torsion classes. Under those conditions they deduce the classical (abelian) Leopoldt conjecture for a totally real field K and prime p from Hida's non-abelian Leopoldt conjecture, without assuming automorphic induction of characters for K/Q.
events.revisions: v1 24 Sep 2014; v2 6 Jul 2016 ('to appear in AJM').
events.delivers: A conditional reduction: classical Leopoldt for totally real K at p, given Hida's non-abelian conjecture and the automorphy-lifting hypotheses. Nothing unconditional.
events.remains: Unconditional Leopoldt for all fields and primes; Hida's non-abelian conjecture and the Galois-representation hypotheses are assumed.
events.doubts: Conditional throughout. Acceptance in AJM is stated only as 'to appear' on arXiv; not verified.
events.direction: Conditional reduction in the conjectured direction: deduces Leopoldt from a stronger non-abelian conjecture.

events.what_happened: A listing on sugaku.net (Mihailescu's author page) includes 'A Conditional Proof of the Leopoldt Conjecture for CM Fields' (2021). The page returned HTTP 403 to my fetch, and the paper is not in the arXiv author listing. Its text, venue, condition and relation to the 2011 and 2014 claims are all unknown. AI involvement cannot be determined: nothing I could read names a system, but I could not read this item.
events.delivers: Unknown. The title says the result is conditional, so presumably a conditional result on CM fields.
events.remains: Unknown.
events.doubts: The title conflicts with the unconditional 2011 and 2014 claims, and the relation is unknown. This is an unopened listing, so no doubt is established.
events.direction: Unknown from the title alone.

events.what_happened: Maksoud, 'On the rank of Leopoldt's and Gross's regulator maps' (arXiv 2201.08203; v1 20 Jan 2022 under the title 'On Leopoldt's and Gross's defects for Artin representations'; v2 16 Feb 2023; Documenta Mathematica 28 (2023) 1441-1471). Abstract: generalizes Waldschmidt's bound on the Leopoldt defect to arbitrary extensions of number fields; proves a similar bound for Gross's defect; proves new cases of Gross's finiteness conjecture (Gross-Kuz'min) beyond the classical abelian case; shows Gross's p-adic regulator has at least half the conjectured rank. The abstract does not state the bound's formula; the paper was not read.
events.revisions: v1 20 Jan 2022 (title 'On Leopoldt's and Gross's defects for Artin representations'); v2 16 Feb 2023; journal Doc. Math. 28 (2023) 1441-1471.
events.delivers: A relative bound on the Leopoldt defect for arbitrary extensions L/K (the abstract says it bounds the defect). By the abstract's own description it bounds the defect and proves no new vanishing of the defect for a specific field.
events.remains: Vanishing of the defect for every number field and prime.

checked_by.what_they_did: Published the paper in volume 28 (2023), pp. 1441-1471

events.direction: Partial bound in the conjectured direction (defect tends to zero).

events.what_happened: Kleine, Documenta Mathematica 2022: if no prime above p splits completely in a Z_p-extension, the vanishing of Iwasawa's mu-invariant implies the weak Leopoldt conjecture for that extension. Kleine notes that this is due to Ueda. Weak Leopoldt is a statement about one Z_p-extension, not Leopoldt's conjecture. Known only from a search snippet; not opened.
events.delivers: Weak Leopoldt for Z_p-extensions under a mu=0 hypothesis. Not Leopoldt's conjecture for any number field.
events.remains: Leopoldt for all number fields and primes.
events.direction: Neighbouring result (weak Leopoldt); does not move the conjecture.

events.what_happened: Ferri and Johnston, 'Applications of representation theory and of explicit units to Leopoldt's conjecture' (arXiv 2301.05700; v1 13 Jan 2023 per the arXiv abstract page, though a search result gave 11 Jan; v2 23 Mar 2026; arXiv comment 'author accepted manuscript incorporating changes after referee reports'; journal reference Res. Number Theory 12, 32 (2026)). Results per the abstract: (i) for Galois L/K with group hypotheses, Leopoldt at p for suitable proper intermediate fields implies Leopoldt at p for L, with relations among the defects; (ii) using Buchmann-Sands and explicit units, for any finite set of primes P there is an infinite family of totally real S3-extensions of Q for which Leopoldt holds at every prime of P.
events.revisions: v1 13 Jan 2023; v2 23 Mar 2026 (after referee reports). Journal reference Res. Number Theory 12, 32 (2026). A search result gave v1 as 11 Jan 2023; the arXiv page gives 13 Jan.
events.delivers: For each finite set of primes P, an infinite family of non-abelian (S3) totally real fields over Q for which Leopoldt holds at every prime of P, plus a reduction lemma for Galois extensions. Not all primes, and not all fields.
events.remains: Leopoldt for every number field at every prime; for the S3 families, every prime outside P; every non-abelian field not reached by the reduction lemma.

checked_by.who: Research in Number Theory (Springer), refereed journal
checked_by.what_they_did: Accepted the paper after referee reports (per the arXiv comment and journal reference)

events.doubts: I read only the abstract page, not the full text, so the S3 family construction and the reduction lemma's hypotheses are not checked. The Springer and PubMed records could not be read, so the journal details rest on the arXiv journal reference.
events.direction: Affirms Leopoldt for named families at named primes, in the conjectured direction; no counterexample.
events.object: Infinite families of totally real S3-extensions of Q, built from Buchmann-Sands units and explicit unit descriptions, for which Leopoldt holds at each prime of a prescribed finite set. These are positive instances, not counterexamples. The construction is not explicit in the abstract; the families are described as infinite and non-abelian.

events.what_happened: Salch, 'Denominators of special values of zeta-functions count KU-local homotopy groups of mod p Moore spectra' (arXiv 2303.09550; one version, 16 Mar 2023). Abstract: for each odd prime p, the orders of the KU-local homotopy groups of the mod p Moore spectrum equal denominators of special values of certain quotients of Dedekind zeta functions of totally real number fields; 'With this observation in hand, we give a cute topological proof of the Leopoldt conjecture for those number fields', by periodicity of KU-local stable homotopy. A search-result excerpt of the body (the PDF could not be decoded) says the fields in its Theorem 5.3 are all abelian and so were already covered by Baker and Brumer, so the novelty is the method. Journal: Rocky Mountain J. Math. 53(3) (2023), per a search summary, not verified.
events.delivers: Per the abstract: Leopoldt at odd primes for the totally real fields in the denominator identity. Per the body excerpt: only abelian families, so no new case. The scope is unresolved between the two.
events.remains: Non-abelian totally real fields, non-totally-real fields, and prime 2 (if the abstract's odd-prime restriction is read literally).
events.time_since_posted: about 3 years 7 months. Searches for comments or reviews found none.
events.doubts: Scope ambiguity between the abstract ('those number fields', read as all totally real fields) and the body excerpt (abelian families only). The body excerpt also reports that the method's extension to non-abelian cases is an open question. No public engagement found.
events.direction: Claims a proof in the conjectured direction for a class whose exact extent is unresolved.

events.what_happened: Mejias Gil and Nickel, arXiv 2401.06045 (posted January 2024). Compares two complexes from equivariant Iwasawa main conjectures for fields that need not be totally real, and shows they are isomorphic in the derived category of Iwasawa modules if weak Leopoldt holds for the relevant Z_p-extension. The exact posting day was not checked; the arXiv number suggests early January. Not opened.
events.delivers: A derived-category isomorphism of two Iwasawa complexes, conditional on weak Leopoldt for a Z_p-extension. Says nothing about Leopoldt's conjecture itself.
events.remains: Leopoldt for every number field and prime.
events.direction: Neighbouring and conditional; does not move the conjecture.

events.what_happened: Dasgupta and Kakde, 'Ranks of Matrices of Logarithms of Algebraic Numbers II: The Matrix Coefficient Conjecture' (arXiv 2408.08178; v1 only, submitted 15 Aug 2024). Formulates the Matrix Coefficient Conjecture (MCC) for singular matrices of logarithms of algebraic numbers, and a p-adic version. Proves that the Structural Rank Conjecture implies MCC. Theorem 3.1: Conjecture 1.2 (the p-adic MCC) implies Leopoldt's conjecture; the introduction also says it implies Gross-Kuz'min. Section 4 gives an unconditional Waldschmidt-Masser-type bound: the ranks of the Leopoldt and Gross regulator matrices are at least half their expected values. The MCC itself is not proved in the paper. A search summary says the authors' auxiliary-polynomial strategy has not yet produced the needed polynomials.
events.revisions: v1 15 Aug 2024 only on arXiv. Published in Advances in Mathematics vol. 487 (1 March 2026), per the Duke publications listing; the publisher page was not opened.
events.delivers: Conditional: if the p-adic Matrix Coefficient Conjecture holds, then Leopoldt's conjecture holds. Unconditional: the half-rank bound on the Leopoldt regulator matrix.
events.remains: Leopoldt, unless the p-adic MCC is proved. The unconditional part is only the half-rank bound.

checked_by.who: Advances in Mathematics (Elsevier), refereed journal, per the Duke publications listing
checked_by.what_they_did: Published as vol. 487 (March 2026), per the Duke listing; the publisher's record was not opened

events.time_since_posted: about 2 years 2 months since arXiv; no citing work located
events.doubts: The implication is conditional on an open conjecture that the paper does not prove. The Duke listing gives no status word; the journal publication is reported only by Duke. No independent reading located.
events.direction: Conditional reduction in the conjectured direction (Leopoldt follows from the p-adic MCC).

events.what_happened: Nguyen Quang Do, 'On Greenberg's generalized conjecture for families of number fields' (arXiv 2505.07529; posted May 2025, revised Oct 2025). Uses Leopoldt as a hypothesis: for a totally real field satisfying Leopoldt's conjecture, the classical and generalized Greenberg conjectures coincide. Also uses Gross-Kuz'min as an assumption in a related statement. Read from a search summary only; not opened.
events.revisions: Posted May 2025; revised Oct 2025 (per search summary).
events.delivers: Nothing on Leopoldt itself; conditional uses of it.
events.remains: Leopoldt for every number field and prime.
events.direction: Conditional use of the conjecture in a neighbouring problem; does not move it.

events.what_happened: Barrera Salazar, Graham and Williams, 'The non-abelian Leopoldt conjecture and equalities of L-invariants' (arXiv 2603.18961; v1 19 Mar 2026, v2 12 Aug 2026). Assuming the non-abelian Leopoldt conjecture (NALC), Hansen's p-adic overconvergent eigenvariety is etale over weight space at non-critical classical points; under a tangent-vector hypothesis, equality of Fontaine-Mazur and automorphic L-invariants for Steinberg-type cuspidal representations; symmetric power lifts with NALC as the only missing assumption. A search summary of the authors' earlier note (arXiv 2108.09191) says NALC for G = Res_{E/Q} SL_2 with E totally real is equivalent to the classical Leopoldt conjecture.
events.delivers: Nothing unconditional about Leopoldt. All results are conditional on NALC, a stronger non-abelian generalization that for one special group is equivalent to Leopoldt.
events.remains: Leopoldt for every number field and prime; the paper does not prove NALC or Leopoldt.
events.time_since_posted: about 7 months (v1). No comments or reviews located.
events.doubts: NALC is a larger hypothesis than Leopoldt for general G, so the paper neither shows nor refutes Leopoldt. The equivalence for SL_2 comes from a search summary of 2108.09191, not from a source opened here.
events.direction: Assumes a generalization of the conjecture; not a result in its direction.

events.what_happened: Hofmann and Johnston, 'Algorithms for p-rationality and for p-saturation of units' (arXiv 2609.15190, submitted 14 Sep 2026). The fetched abstract: algorithms deciding whether a number field K is p-rational without computing the class number or full unit group; a new algorithm for unconditional verification of unit groups. A search-result excerpt says that, assuming Gras's Conjecture 3.5, the algorithm verifies Leopoldt for a fixed K at all but finitely many primes. The fetched abstract does not mention Leopoldt or Gross's Conjecture 3.5, so that excerpt is unconfirmed.
events.delivers: At most per-field computational verification, and per the unconfirmed excerpt only conditional on Gras's Conjecture 3.5. Says nothing about the conjecture for all fields.
events.remains: Leopoldt for every number field and prime.
events.directly_checkable: The unit-group verification is a per-field computation; I did not check any output.
events.doubts: Whether the Leopoldt verification claim (conditional on Gras's Conjecture 3.5) is in the paper is unconfirmed. Per-field checks do not move the universal statement.
events.direction: Per-field instances only; no direction for the conjecture as stated.

disputes.summary: Mihailescu's CM claim is described as 'CM-extensions of Q' in Wikipedia (last edited 21 July 2026, per the fetch summary) and as 'CM number fields K' in the arXiv abstract of 1105.4544 (v4). The arXiv wording is broader than the encyclopedia's.

Salch's abstract says 'a cute topological proof of the Leopoldt conjecture for those number fields' (totally real fields, odd p), but the body excerpt seen in search says the fields in its Theorem 5.3 are abelian and so already known. The two readings differ on whether anything new is claimed.

Mihailescu's unconditional CM claims (2011 v4, 2014) and a 2021 listing titled 'A Conditional Proof of the Leopoldt Conjecture for CM Fields' appear to conflict. The relation between them is unknown because the 2021 text was not readable.

summary: Nothing in the sources I could read settles Leopoldt's conjecture for all number fields and primes, and no source names an AI system involved in any Leopoldt work. Established cases: Ax and Brumer (1965-67) cover abelian extensions of Q and of imaginary quadratic fields; Waldschmidt's bound (1981) gives a defect bound that forces zero defect only for small unit rank. Mihailescu has the largest set of claims. He posted a general claim for all number fields (0905.1274, May 2009) and claims for solvable K/Q and totally real K/Q with p split completely (0909.2738, Sep 2009), and a claim for CM fields (1105.4544, May 2011; current v4 Feb 2016; the CM claim is repeated in 1403.7331, Mar 2014). The 2009 papers were withdrawn in Feb 2015; v3 of the 2011 paper was withdrawn and v4 reposted. The CM argument depends on a claim of mu=0 for CM Z_p-extensions, which is stronger than the Leopoldt statement (its cyclotomic case is Iwasawa's mu=0 for CM fields; my understanding, unverified here, is that this is open in general). A 2021 listing with the title 'conditional' exists only on sugaku.net and was unreadable to me. Across 15 years, I found no referee report, journal acceptance or published critique of any Mihailescu claim. The Wikipedia article (last edited 21 July 2026, per the fetch summary) reports the CM claim as 'announced' and does not mention any of the 2023 to 2026 partial results, though a recheck fetch was summary-level. Partial results: Ferri and Johnston (posted Jan 2023, journal reference Res. Number Theory 2026) give infinitely many non-abelian S3 totally real fields with Leopoldt at each prime of a prescribed finite set, and a reduction lemma; Khare and Thorne (2014) deduce classical Leopoldt from Hida's non-abelian conjecture under automorphy hypotheses; Maksoud (2022) generalizes the defect bound. Salch (Mar 2023) gives a topological proof claim whose scope is unresolved between an abstract for all totally real fields and a body excerpt that says the fields are abelian. Within the window (from 26 Jan 2024): Dasgupta and Kakde (Aug 2024) show a p-adic Matrix Coefficient Conjecture would imply Leopoldt, conditional on that conjecture, published in Advances in Mathematics vol. 487 per Duke; Barrera Salazar, Graham and Williams (Mar 2026) assume a non-abelian generalization of the conjecture; Hofmann and Johnston (Sep 2026) give per-field algorithms, with a Leopoldt claim I could not confirm. The AI search (explicit AI terms, AI-math trackers and lab announcements) found AI results on other problems (Erdos unit-distance, Jacobian conjecture news, AI-number-theory surveys) and none naming Leopoldt, so none_found is true on every event. Close calls: the Mihailescu CM claim (a restricted resolution if it holds) versus withdrawal, recasting and no reading; Salch's scope; and whether Ferri-Johnston's finitely-many-primes families count for anything in the judging pass. Withdrawn or unverified items are recorded as events with their evidence, not dropped.
competing_reading: Read Mihailescu's CM claim (v4 Feb 2016, unchallenged for about ten years, reported as 'announced' on Wikipedia) as a real, restricted resolution for every CM field; read Salch's abstract as covering all totally real fields. On that reading the problem was partly solved from 2011 to 2014 and the in-window events add nothing to a settled status. Against it: the author withdrew earlier versions and recast the CM claim as conditional in a 2021 listing, no referee report or journal acceptance was found, and the CM argument needs mu=0 for CM Z_p-extensions, a claim that, on my understanding, is stronger than the Leopoldt statement. Ferri and Johnston's families and Dasgupta and Kakde's conditional implication are, on the other reading, the only positive in-window material, and neither moves the conjecture as stated.
what_would_settle_it: (1) A referee report, journal acceptance or published critique of Mihailescu's CM argument (1105.4544 v4 and 1403.7331), and the text and condition of the 2021 'Conditional Proof' (readable copy needed; sugaku returned 403). (2) The mu=0 companion papers (1105.1970, 1409.3114) and whether mu=0 for cyclotomic Z_p-extensions of CM fields is known. (3) The readable body of Salch 2303.09550, especially Theorem 1.3 and 5.3, to settle whether any non-abelian field is covered. (4) The published Ferri-Johnston text (Springer page, redirected to a login) for the S3 families and the reduction lemma's hypotheses. (5) Any proof of the p-adic Matrix Coefficient Conjecture (Dasgupta and Kakde) or of Hida's non-abelian conjecture. (6) A current survey or the Wikipedia article's own sources stating the general status.

judgement.why: The statement is universal over all number fields and primes, so restricted classes (abelian, S5/S3 families at given primes, CM) are cases and defect bounds are bounds. Every post-snapshot event is either a conditional reduction (Dasgupta-Kakde: p-adic MCC implies Leopoldt), a conditional use of the conjecture or a generalization (Nguyen, Barrera Salazar-Graham-Williams), or per-field computation (Hofmann-Johnston, instances). Dasgupta-Kakde's unconditional half-rank bound reproduces the Waldschmidt-type half-rank bound already known pre-snapshot, so I scored it none rather than bound. Mihailescu's 2009 papers are withdrawn (knocked_down); his CM claims stay as doubtful unreviewed cases. Mejias Gil-Nickel is dated January 2024 at month precision, so it cannot be placed either side of 26 January; it is none regardless. No AI system appears in any event.
judgement.doubts: Dasgupta-Kakde's half-rank bound: if it is stronger than Waldschmidt/Maksoud in some respect the record does not show, it would be a post-snapshot bound. Brumer/Buchmann-Sands/Waldschmidt verification rests on journal publication reported via citing sources, not opened.
